liam_dev: Noticed flaky timeouts + connection leak in sampleapp when running long syncs on Pixel 8 emulator (Android 14). Happens only when we use Retrofit.enqueue() from a WorkManager worker that batches a few dozen small requests.

tara_sdk: Hmm. Are you using the default OkHttp Dispatcher? If maxRequests is unlimited, parallelism can exhaust HTTP/2 streams and cause weird ECONNRESET behavior.

liam_dev: We left dispatcher defaults. Logs show a bunch of: 

```
W/OkHttp: A connection to /10.0.2.2 was leaked. Did you forget to close a response body?
I/Network: streamAllocation timed out waiting for a connection
E/Network: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: timeout
```

jeff_eng: Two things to check: (1) ensure ResponseBody.close() always called if you use enqueue (onFailure/onResponse). (2) prefer a coroutine Call adapter so the worker can cancel properly instead of fire-and-forget enqueue that keeps sockets open.

liam_dev: We're using the Kotlin Coroutine adapter but some legacy workers still call `service.syncItems().enqueue(...)`. Legacy code got copied into the sample branch.

mike_sre: From infra side: when emulator/device sleeps, TCP keepalive behaves weirdly and pooled sockets can be torn. If many in-flight requests pile up they try to reuse dead sockets. Tightening connect/read timeouts and reducing dispatcher.maxRequests helped us before. Example config we use: 

```
val dispatcher = Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 8; maxRequestsPerHost = 4 }
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .dispatcher(dispatcher)
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .readTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .callTimeout(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()
```

tara_sdk: Also consider setting connectionPool.evictionDuration shorter for mobile (e.g., 5s) so stale sockets are closed quicker, but test for battery impact. And add a leak-detection test in the CI emulator matrix.

liam_dev: Good call. I tried adding the dispatcher limits + explicit close() and swapped one worker to `withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { service.syncItems().await() }`. That stopped the leaks in my local Pixel 8 runs.

jeff_eng: If you convert workers to use suspending calls, don't forget to call `.cancel()` on the retrofit Call if coroutine is cancelled; best practice is to use a Call.await() adapter that ties cancellation to Call.cancel().

liam_dev: Pushed a tiny sample: `android/samples/emulator-conn-pool-leak-fix`. CI run triggered.

ci-bot: CI: samples/emulator-conn-pool-leak-fix build queued (job #5487).

mike_sre: One more quick note: when using HTTP/2 multiplexing, per-host limits matter less but Android platform quirks still apply. Keep an eye on Traceview for blocked threads during large syncs.

tara_sdk: We should document recommended OkHttp defaults for mobile SDK users: dispatcher limits, short pool eviction, and use coroutine-aware adapters in onboarding. Filing a short doc in /docs/devex/okhttp-mobile-best-practices.

liam_dev: Thanks all. I'll land the sample and open the doc PR with examples + CI test.
